    AI Overview
    The Artemis 2 mission is estimated to cost approximately $4.1 billion for a single launch, according to a 2021 audit by NASA's Office of Inspector General. This expense covers the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule. Total spending for the entire Artemis program through 2025 is projected at roughly $93 billion. 
    • Cost Drivers: The high cost is largely due to the development of the SLS rocket and the Orion capsule.
    • Cost per Launch: Multiple sources estimate the cost per launch for Artemis I through IV to be between $4 billion and $4.2 billion.
    • Program Scope:
      The overall Artemis program, aimed at returning humans to the Moon and establishing a long-term presence, is estimated to cost over $90 billion through 2025.
    • Funding: The program is primarily funded by U.S. taxpayers, with additional support from international partners such as the European Space Agency (ESA).

    AI Overview
    Each individual Artemis II mission launch, including the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft, is estimated to cost over $4 billion. This mission is part of the broader Artemis program, which is projected to cost roughly $93 billion through 2025. 
    Key Cost Details for Artemis II: 
    • Per-Launch Cost: Approximately $4.1 billion per mission.
    • Total Program Cost: The overall Artemis program, spanning over a decade, is estimated to cost around $93 billion.
    • Components: This high cost covers the development and operation of the SLS rocket, the Orion capsule, ground systems, and testing
      .
    • Funding Source: The program is primarily funded by the United States government via NASA, with support from international partners. 
    These figures are based on reports from the NASA Inspector General and the Government Accountability Office.
